items.detail: Wall Street ripped higher to open August: the **S&P 500 jumped 1.48% to 7,600.50**, the **Nasdaq surged 2.1%** and the **Dow rose ~1.3% to a record close**, more than reversing Friday's cautious tone.
items.why: President Trump said he called off a planned strike on Iran and reopened talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil sharply lower and reigniting risk appetite as a heavy earnings week began.

items.detail: Oil violently reversed last month's war premium, with **Brent tumbling below $83** and **WTI settling near $78.93, down close to 7%** to a three-week low — a stark turn after both contracts rose more than **20% in July**.
items.why: Trump's decision to postpone strikes and pursue a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz eased the supply-shock fears that had driven the July crude spike.

items.detail: **Big Tech led the advance**, with communications-services and software names powering the Nasdaq's 2.1% gain as the AI-capex trade shifted back to offense following Amazon's blowout AWS print last week.
items.why: Cheaper oil lowered the inflation and rates overhang just as investors leaned back into megacaps at the start of a dense corporate earnings calendar.

items.detail: Focus now turns to **Friday's July jobs report** and a packed week of earnings, the next test of whether the oil-driven rebound can extend against a still-hawkish Fed that held rates at **3.5%–3.75%**.

Indian equities surged for a **fourth straight session to a five-month high**: the **Nifty 50 jumped 390.70 points (1.60%) to 24,774.30** and the **Sensex added 544.39 points (0.70%) to 78,639.03**, a decisive break above last week's ~24,350 range.
items.why: A sharp slide in crude prices after Trump paused strikes on Iran eased India's import-bill and inflation worries, the exact overhang flagged as the market's chief risk just days earlier.

items.detail: Leadership flipped hard from last week: **Nifty IT was the top sector, surging 2.68%**, with FMCG (+1.72%), metals (+1.55%), auto (+1.48%) and PSU banks (+1.41%) all higher and every major index bar media in the green.
items.why: Indian software rebounded sharply from its prior >2% slide as the global tech rally and firmer risk sentiment revived buying in the beaten-down sector.

items.detail: Flows turned supportive on both sides: **FIIs bought ₹922 crore** and **DIIs added ₹1,517 crore** in the cash segment, a notable pickup in foreign appetite after weeks of cautious, DII-led support.
items.why: The crude pullback and easing Middle East tensions coaxed foreign investors back in, complementing steady domestic buying to broaden the rally.

items.detail: Benchmarks are set to **open flat to slightly lower on Tuesday**, with GIFT Nifty down ~6 points to 24,646, as subdued Asian cues test whether the four-day, oil-fueled run can extend.
**Bitcoin slipped to around $62,643** and **Ether eased to roughly $1,840** on Monday, both drifting lower and failing to join the equity and oil-driven risk rally even as geopolitical tension eased.
items.why: The de-escalation that lifted stocks and sank oil failed to spark crypto momentum, as a still-hawkish Fed and stalled US regulatory progress kept speculative capital sidelined.

items.detail: A fresh homegrown headwind emerged as the **US Senate delayed the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act**, denting hopes for a near-term institutional-grade regulatory framework.
items.why: The legislative delay removed a potential positive catalyst, leaving crypto without the regulatory clarity investors had been counting on to draw fresh institutional capital.

items.detail: Spot Bitcoin ETFs are showing tentative signs of a thaw: **2026 cumulative net outflows narrowed to ~$4.84B** from roughly $5.4B in July, with **three consecutive weeks of positive inflows** breaking the year's persistent bleed.
items.why: A modest return of institutional demand is beginning to offset the record outflows seen earlier in 2026, though flows remain fragile and macro-driven.

items.detail: The macro calendar now dominates: with the **Fed holding at 3.5%–3.75%** and the **next FOMC decision on September 16**, traders are eyeing upcoming CPI/jobs prints and the August 27–29 Jackson Hole symposium as the key swing factors.

crossCuttingTheme: Oil was the master switch this session: Trump calling off Iran strikes sent Brent below $83 and WTI down ~7%, collapsing the war-driven inflation premium and igniting record-setting US equity gains and a five-month-high Nifty rally led by rate-sensitive IT and autos — yet crypto sat out the risk-on move, weighed by a still-hawkish Fed and a stalled US regulatory bill.
